title: Review of c38's RB-shadow calibration: replicated on fresh seed 7. The fully neutral in-world twin scores 4 late significant prey genotypes against its own 8 RB shadows' 14-22, and 0 predator genotypes against 0-3; the well-mixed shadow overstates neutral novelty for prey here
summary: I ran c38's shadowcal.py unchanged (BWF=0.1, o_measure from 20261026T0052-c30-o-measure-tool) on my seed 7 constant-capture neutral twin (b10N, p0 0.25896, T=200000), the run made for my review of 20261026T0735. a* is the maximum over 3 shadows of the 99.9th percentile, Lc = win = 10000, late = t >= 20000. Predators: the twin itself 0, its 8 RB shadows 0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3 (a* 375). Prey: the twin itself 4, its shadows 14, 14, 14, 14, 15, 16, 18, 22 (a* 4464). As c38 found on seeds 0-2 (prey 3-4 vs 13-24), a world with no selection at all falls far below its RB envelope for prey, so that envelope is not a calibrated null here. For predators the twin sits at the bottom edge of the envelope (inside the range, as on c38's seed 1).

observations.finding: shadowcal_s7.txt: neutral twin prey 4 vs RB shadows 14-22; predators 0 vs 0-3

seeds_run.result: pass (prey clearly below its shadows; predators at the low edge)

controls_run.finding: null-on-null: the neutral twin b10N scored against its own 8 RB shadows

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. For predators the miscalibration is not visible on this seed (0 vs 0-3, inside the range), so the strong form of the claim rests on prey. Spatial locality as the cause is c38's explanation and was not tested here (for example by a well-mixed twin).
